author: miguel.santos
title: Just joined the community — hi from Lisbon!
body:
Hey everyone, I'm Miguel, joining from Lisbon. I've been working with Liferay for about 18 months — started on a 7.4 project doing classic OSGi modules, but I've been spending most of my time lately on Headless APIs and Objects. The shift from JSP/portlet thinking to pure REST consumers has been refreshing, even if it took a while to internalize.

Right now I'm building an internal HR portal where employees can submit time-off requests through a Custom Element CX that talks to a Forum Object on the back end. I'm sure I'll have plenty of questions about edge cases (workflow integration, scoping, OAuth flows for the JS client) and I hope I can also contribute back on the topics where I've burned enough hours to have an opinion.

author: nadia.ahmed
title: OAuth2 token expiration handling with custom providers
body:
I'm integrating Liferay with a custom OAuth2 provider (not Google/Azure — an internal IdP based on Keycloak). The initial login flow works fine: tokens come back, the user gets authenticated, and we can call protected REST endpoints. The problem starts about an hour later, when the access token expires.

From what I can tell, Liferay's OAuth2 client module receives the 401 response but doesn't automatically exchange the refresh_token for a new access_token. Users just get bumped to the login page mid-session, which is obviously not great for an SPA experience. I've looked through com.liferay.oauth2.provider.* but I'm not sure if the refresh logic lives there or in a separate filter.

Has anyone wired up automatic refresh against a custom IdP successfully? Is there a hook/extension point I should be overriding, or do I need to write a custom AutoLogin implementation that handles the refresh handshake?

author: oliver.brandt
title: Folder structure for multi-environment Client Extensions
body:
Our client-extensions/ directory has grown to about 22 CXs across 4 environments (dev, qa, staging, prod) and it's becoming hard to reason about. We currently keep one folder per CX with environment-specific values inline in client-extension.yaml, but that means a config tweak for prod ends up touching the same file devs commit changes to constantly. Merge conflicts every Monday.

I've seen a couple of approaches floating around — keeping a single client-extension.yaml per CX with property placeholders that get substituted at build time from an env-specific properties file, or splitting the CX folder itself into shared/ + per-env/ subfolders. Both feel like they're working around the tooling rather than embracing it.

For teams running 15+ CXs, what's the structure that actually scales? Curious whether anyone has tried generating CX folders from a template (Cookiecutter / Yeoman style) so the consistency is enforced by tooling instead of convention.

author: priya.kapoor
title: Bulk Object Entry import via CSV in the admin UI
body:
Today, the only ways to bulk-load Object Entries are the Headless Batch Engine API and the *.batch-engine-data.json files in site-initializers. Both require a developer in the loop. For business admins who just need to seed 500 rows from an Excel export, that's a real friction point — they end up shipping the CSV to engineering and waiting a day.

What I'd love to see is a simple Import CSV button on the Object detail page in Control Panel that maps columns to Object fields (with a preview step) and accepts the file directly. The mapping could even be saved as a named profile so recurring imports become one click. The Batch Engine is already there under the hood; this would just be a UI on top.

I know there are workarounds (custom workflow, dedicated admin portlets, etc.), but for adoption among non-technical site admins, a first-class UI matters. Has this been discussed at any of the recent DXP roadmap reviews?

author: carla.rivera
title: Workflow Designer not triggering after publish
body:
I built a 4-step approval workflow in the Kaleo Designer (Initial → Manager Review → Finance Review → Approved/Rejected), published it from the UI, and assigned it to my PurchaseOrder Object via the Workflow tab. Entries are getting created without errors, but the workflow never seems to fire — no notifications, no task assignments, nothing in the My Workflow Tasks portlet.

What's really throwing me off is that the Workflow Logs panel is completely empty. Not just no tasks — no log entries at all, as if the workflow definition wasn't even associated with the Object. I double-checked the assignment in Control Panel → Objects → PurchaseOrder → Workflow and the dropdown clearly shows my workflow selected.

Where would you start debugging this? I'm wondering if it's a permissions issue (the entry creator can't initiate the workflow?), a transaction isolation thing (the workflow lookup happens in a different transaction than the entry insert?), or just a stale cache. The site has been restarted twice with no change.

author: frank.tanaka
title: Lessons from a 6-month migration from 7.4 to 2025.Q4
body:
We just wrapped up a long upgrade from Liferay 7.4 GA1 to 2025.Q4 for a 200k-user customer portal — six months of testing, three production rehearsals, and one very tense weekend. Now that the dust has settled, here are the things I wish someone had hammered into me on day one.

The biggest surprise was the OSGi module compatibility cliff. About 40% of our 60 custom modules needed at least one code change beyond a recompile — mostly around removed taglibs, the new headless modules replacing legacy REST endpoints, and Service Builder regenerating differently. Plan for a full audit and reserve at least 2-3 weeks for it. Don't trust that a clean Gradle build means "it works".

The other under-discussed area is data migration for Custom Fields. We had ~3M entries with expando attributes that we wanted to move to Object fields. The official upgrade process doesn't touch these — you need a custom upgrade step or batch script. Do it before flipping production traffic, because doing it live with users actively writing is a nightmare. Happy to share our batch scripts if useful.

author: grace.obi
title: Persistent sessions across multiple Liferay nodes
body:
We're running a 4-node Liferay cluster behind nginx with sticky sessions (ip_hash). It works fine for the happy path — a user lands on node A, all their requests go back to A, performance is great. The problem is failover: when node A is taken out (rolling restart, autoscaling event, whatever), the user's session is just gone. They get bounced to the login screen mid-action, which has been our #1 complaint in the post-rollout user feedback.

I've read about Tomcat's session replication via DeltaManager but the docs warn that it doesn't play well with Liferay's session attributes (some of which aren't Serializable). Then there's the option of moving sessions to Redis or a JDBC-backed session store, but I'm not sure which is the supported path on 2025.Q4 — the documentation I've found is mostly written for 7.4.

For folks running multi-node clusters in production today, what's the actual setup? Specifically interested in: what session store you're using, whether you needed any portal-ext tweaks, and how big the performance hit is. Also whether 2025.Q4 changed anything here vs 7.4.

author: elena.petrov
title: Caching strategies for high-traffic forum-style sites
body:
I'd love to hear how others are tuning caches for read-heavy public sites (forums, knowledge bases, news sites). We're prepping for an expected 10x traffic bump this fall and our current setup — default Ehcache + a thin Varnish layer — was put together kind of opportunistically a few years ago. I want to revisit it with intention rather than just bumping Xmx and hoping.

Specifically I'm curious about three layers: (1) Liferay's internal entity caches — are people still tweaking ehcache-cluster-link.xml or has 2025.Q4 moved to something else? (2) Fragment / page output caches — for anonymous traffic on cacheable pages, what's the realistic hit rate you're getting in production? (3) CDN edge caching for HTML — we've been afraid to do this because of personalization, but the recent CDN docs hint at vary-by-segment which would unblock us.

Less interested in benchmarks (every workload is different) and more in pragmatic guidance: "do this before this, watch out for X gotcha, this knob looks tempting but is a trap." War stories welcome.
